_meta.method: Targeted web research of major Taiwanese Chan/Zen institutions, cross-referenced with official sites and Wikipedia. Taiwanese Chan treated as Zen for taxonomy.
_meta.coverageEstimate: High for the four major Chan institutions (Dharma Drum, Chung Tai, Fo Guang Shan, Linji-Rinzai). Lower for smaller independent zendos and Sanbo Zen affiliates.
knownGaps: Hundreds of small Chung Tai branch meditation centers across Taiwan not enumerated.
Numerous Fo Guang Shan branch temples with Chan halls not enumerated.
Smaller independent Chan groups, Sanbo Zen affiliates and Yuanjue Hall not separately verified.

places.name: Dharma Drum Mountain World Center for Buddhist Education
places.address: No. 555, Fagu Rd., Jinshan District, New Taipei City 20842, Taiwan
places.notes: Dharma Drum Mountain’s main monastery and education center at No. 555 Fagu Rd., Jinshan. The official 2026 calendar lists Chan retreats at this site, including Oct. 24–31; these are registered retreats with prior-training requirements, not drop-in sittings. The monastery’s official history identifies it as a Chan institution.

places.name: Nung Chan Monastery (Water-Moon Dharma Center)
places.address: No. 89, Lane 65, Daye Rd., Beitou District, Taipei City 112, Taiwan
places.notes: Dharma Drum Mountain monastery at No. 89, Lane 65, Daye Rd., Beitou. Its official current page advertises Chan sitting, a Wednesday half-day Chan session, and other practice activities. Official DDM history says the monastery was established by Dongchu in 1975. Check the current event page for registration and access details.

places.name: Chung Tai Chan Monastery
places.address: No. 2, Zhongtai Rd., Puli Township, Nantou County 545, Taiwan
places.notes: Main Linji Chan monastery of Chung Tai Shan in Puli, Nantou. The official history says the larger monastery was inaugurated in 2001, following the founding abbot’s 1987 Lingquan Monastery, where Chan-7 retreats were held. Current official listings include meditation-center classes; the main monastery offers guided tours by reservation, with areas available depending on the day’s events. Tour access does not establish open public meditation at the main site.

places.name: Fo Guang Shan Monastery (Chan Hall)
places.lineage: Chan / Linji (Fo Guang Shan, Humanistic Buddhism)
places.address: No. 153, Xingtian Rd., Dashu District, Kaohsiung City 840, Taiwan
places.notes: Fo Guang Shan headquarters at No. 153 Xingtian Rd., Dashu, Kaohsiung. Founded in 1967 by Venerable Master Hsing Yun. The monastery describes an onsite Meditation Hall used for Chan practice and cultivation retreats; the hall has capacity for over 400 practitioners; its grounds reopened to the public to some extent, but the source does not establish daily public access to the hall or a current retreat calendar. Describe as a broader Humanistic Buddhist monastery with Chan facilities.

places.name: Linji Huguo Chan Temple
places.address: No. 9 Yumen St., Zhongshan District, Taipei City, Taiwan
places.notes: Historic Chan temple at No. 9 Yumen St., Zhongshan District, Taipei. Taipei’s tourism authority lists daily visitor hours of 08:30–11:00 and 13:00–17:00; its official history says construction ran from 1900 to 1911. Treat as a historic visitor temple. No current meditation schedule or present-day institutional lineage was verified.

places.name: Dharma Drum Retreat Center (Sanyi Branch)
places.notes: Dharma Drum branch retreat / DILA campus; one of multiple DDM education centers across Taiwan.
